title: `additionalProperties`
description: Controls whether an object accepts keys that are not declared in its properties map.
question: Is each object's additional-properties policy preserved at the capture boundary?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP tool schemas declaring additionalProperties.
known_issues: A changed policy can make a downstream caller reject valid extension keys or send keys the server rejects.
why: Object openness is part of the parameter contract. Changing it can alter which calls validate before they reach the server.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: Pydantic model generation rewrites additionalProperties on several object boundaries, changing whether undeclared keys are accepted.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions wraps each inputSchema as jsonSchema({...inputSchema, properties: inputSchema.properties ?? {}, additionalProperties: false}), so every tool's root object is closed to undeclared keys although the server set no policy there. Nested objects keep the server's policy.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` rebuilds each schema as `ParametersSchema(properties, required, additionalProperties)` and defaults `additionalProperties` to `false` when the server omits it, so every tool gains a top-level `additionalProperties: false`.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: the ChatModel default `use_strict_tool_schema=True` runs `to_strict_json_schema` on the rebuilt input model, which adds `additionalProperties: false` to every object, including `create_report`, its `config` and each `sections` item, where the server set nothing.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`, which sets `additionalProperties: false` on every object, including the ones the source left open.

summary: A framework that regenerates the input schema from its own model class can change additionalProperties on the root and nested object schemas.
